Emma — thanks for the clear asks, and great meeting yesterday. Attached is a concise commercial sketch and a TCO worksheet (optimize_pricing_model_v3.xlsx) that breaks down per-token economics across hosted vs Dedicated for three scenarios: no optimizations, caching + batching, and caching + batching + 8-bit quantization.

Top-line summary for your committee:
- Hosted (no commit): baseline token cost X. At 1.5M tokens/day the per-token price is higher due to variable infra — expect ~20–28% higher unit cost vs a modest commit.
- Dedicated reserve (3 month term, commit band outlined in sheet): reduces unit cost by ~30–45% depending on commit band and allowable burst.
- Apply KV prefix caching and continuous batching: estimated token savings of 15–30% effective (depends on prompt repetitiveness).
- Add 8-bit quantization (recommended for stateless generation and many encoder-decoder workloads): additional 18–25% cpu/GPU cost reduction on supported model variants. Combined you can see up to ~40–55% reduction in per-token infra spend vs baseline in our model.

Caveats / constraints:
- 8-bit quantized variants introduce a small latency variance (p99 delta ~8–12ms) on current gen GPUs for long context (3–4k). Karthik — I’m tagging you to confirm memory/kv-cache behavior for the 4k context case.
- Caching effectiveness depends heavily on prompt/template stability — the sheet includes a sensitivity tab.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send a slim commercial offer (three commit bands + pilot credits) — see attached draft PDF.
2) Karthik to confirm quantization constraints and recommended model pinning for SiftScale.
3) Connor to coordinate pilot ops checklist and expected start date if we proceed.

I can also join your procurement call at 3pm PT if useful.

Dylan / Emma — quick technical note on quantization and caching for a 4k chat workload. Quoted below for context.

On Fri, 7 Sep 2028 at 10:05 AM Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com> wrote:
> 
> - Add 8-bit quantization (recommended for stateless generation and many encoder-decoder workloads): additional 18–25% cpu/GPU cost reduction on supported model variants.
> - Caveats / constraints: 8-bit quantized variants introduce a small latency variance (p99 delta ~8–12ms) on current gen GPUs for long context (3–4k). Karthik — I’m tagging you to confirm memory/kv-cache behavior for the 4k context case.

Notes:
- We recommend 8-bit quantization for the inference pipelines where the model remains in a single host memory region (no frequent sharding across GPUs). For a 4k context with active KV cache, two things matter: (1) KV memory fit in device/cache, and (2) kernel choices for attention.
- For SiftScale's expected 1.5M tokens/day, if you use a single-GPU serving slice with KV caching enabled, 8-bit quantization should be safe provided you pin to the quantized model we ship (we've validated up to 4k with the 8-bit kernels on A100/NVIDIA 2xxx-series).
- If you plan to use multi-GPU sharding for throughput, we recommend either (a) mixed precision (16-bit) for the sharded path, or (b) split the workload: quantized instances for high-throughput stateless calls and 16-bit sharded instances for long-history chat. This hybrid approach preserves latency SLOs while delivering cost wins.

Operational tradeoffs:
- Expect slightly higher variance at tail latencies for quantized hosts. We can mitigate by keeping a small pool of 16-bit warm hosts as a fallback for p99-sensitive requests.
- Batching is most effective when request sizes are predictable; continuous batching with a short max-wait (10–15ms) tends to give the best cost/latency balance for conversational traffic.

I can provide a recommended runbook (quant-recs-2028-09-07.md) with explicit model pins and rollout checklist if you want to include it in procurement.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Emma / Procurement — following up with a short, committee-ready sketch and a recommended pilot structure. See attached PDF and the TCO sheet. Key points below you can present today: 

Offer (3-month pilot) — SiftScale (1.5M tokens/day avg):
- Option A (No commit / Hosted): month-to-month. Unit price: baseline price (see sheet). Pilot credit: $10k Redwood credit. Pros: fastest start. Cons: higher unit cost.
- Option B (Pilot commit band — recommended): commit to 3 months / 45M tokens total. Redwood provides 30% unit discount + $25k pilot credits earmarked for Optimize toolkit professional configuration (caching policy + quantization verification).
- Option C (Dedicated reserve / Short-term): locked 3-month Dedicated slice with guaranteed throughput. Unit price: lowest. Requires procurement lead time and contractual SLA.

Technical guardrails we recommend shipping with the pilot:
- Start with hybrid serving: quantized 8-bit instances for stateless generation, 16-bit sharded instances for long-history chat until we validate p99s.
- Enable prefix KV caching on canonical prompts/templates — we’ll provide a short runbook and a caching policy that you can apply via Redwood Console.

Commercial ask & next step:
- If you pick Option B, sign a one-page MSA addendum + the pilot SOW (I will send DocuSign). Deal team proposes a 12% discretionary discount cap beyond the 30% pilot concession; further concessions require AE+Manager approval.
- I’m available at 3pm PT if Procurement wants to discuss the pilot sketch.

Thanks — looking forward to getting SiftScale on pilot.

Best,
